summary: 2 of 4 claims confirmed against the chapter. 1 contradicted. 1 unsupported.

results.claimText: The zeroth law of thermodynamics says that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, then they are also in thermal equilibrium with each other.
results.explanation: The chapter explicitly defines the Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics using this exact statement.
results.quote: two systems in thermal equilibrium with a third system separately are in thermal equilibrium with each other

results.claimText: The Kelvin-Planck statement of the second law says that no process is possible whose sole result is the absorption of heat from a reservoir and the complete conversion of that heat into work.
results.explanation: The text gives the Kelvin-Planck statement word-for-word, asserting that no process can absorb heat from a reservoir and completely convert it into work as its sole result.
results.quote: No process is possible whose sole result is the absorption of heat from a reservoir and the complete conversion of the heat into work.

results.claimText: A perfect engine that converts all absorbed heat into work without any other side effect is still allowed by the second law of thermodynamics, which only limits real engines.
results.explanation: The Kelvin-Planck statement explicitly denies the possibility of a perfect heat engine converting all absorbed heat into work without any other effect.
results.quote: No process is possible whose sole result is the absorption of heat from a reservoir and the complete conversion of the heat into work.

results.claimText: Thermal conductivity is highest in gases because their molecules are spaced farthest apart, so they transfer heat more efficiently than liquids or solids.
results.explanation: The text lists thermal conductivity in a summary table of physical quantities but does not compare thermal conductivity values or heat transfer efficiency across gases, liquids, and solids.
